title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups PR #249 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #249 (frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges. Everything else in that review passed cleanly: static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc/profit-target-wording), backend coverage (99.95%, 1139 passed), frontend coverage (statements 99.73%/branches 99.21%/functions 99.74%/lines 99.79%, 745 passed), the persisted e2e suite (21/21 passing, including the 3 new specs), the seeding-via-API approach (isolated by a distinct fixture ticker (TSLA) not used by any other spec, closed before the block's own first assertion, single-worker/non-parallel config rules out cross-file races), and the task's `decisions` entry (accurately reflects the actual 8-10-week due window in `app/api/routers/portfolio.py` and the 9-week choice already used by the mocked-test fixture).

checklist.step: `frontend/tests/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts`'s new `isoDateWeeksAgo` helper is line-for-line identical to the existing `isoDateWeeksAgo` in `frontend/tests/mocks/handlers.ts` (added by PR #248 for the mocked-test `dueTradeFixture`). Both compute an ISO date N weeks in the past for the same reason (landing a fixture inside the backend's 8-10-week follow-up-due window). Worth extracting to a small shared test utility if a third near-identical copy ever appears; currently only two, in two different test layers (MSW mock handlers for vitest vs. Playwright e2e fixtures), so the coupling tradeoff of sharing across those layers now is arguable rather than clear-cut -- non-blocking.

task-worker reported one flaky timeout in `frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx` on its first vitest run of this PR's changes, which then passed clean on rerun and in isolation. pr-reviewer investigated: this file is entirely untouched by PR #249's diff (the PR only touches `frontend/tests/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts`, `docs/architecture/Testing.md`, and task JSON files), so the flake can't be something this PR introduced or exacerbated. Re-ran the file in isolation 13 times and the full vitest suite 3 times (16 runs total) with zero reproductions -- no evidence of a genuine recurring pre-existing flake, most likely a one-off environmental fluke (e.g. sandbox scheduling jitter) rather than a real timing race in the test or component. Recorded here rather than dropped, per CLAUDE.md's 'would this be lost if nobody re-read this PR' bar: if this timeout recurs on a future run of this file, this entry gives the next investigator a starting point (13+3 clean reruns already ruled out) instead of re-litigating from zero.

The new `test.describe.serial('portfolio: due-for-follow-up review flow', ...)` block in `frontend/tests/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts` has no tolerance for a leftover unreviewed trade from an earlier interrupted run, unlike the sibling 'view, add, and delete a position' block in the same file, whose own doc comment explains it tolerates a pre-existing MSFT position specifically because `playwright.config.ts`'s webServer 'only guarantees a clean database at the start of a whole `yarn test:e2e` invocation, not before each individual spec file.' If test 1 or 2 of the new block fails, leaving the `beforeAll`-seeded TSLA trade unreviewed and due, and the suite is then re-run against a still-alive webServer (e.g. `yarn test:e2e:ui` interactive debugging, which keeps the webServer running across reruns -- not the routine `make e2e`/`yarn test:e2e` path, which always wipes `e2e.db` and restarts both webServers fresh per `reuseExistingServer: false`), `seedDueForFollowUpTrade` seeds a second unreviewed TSLA due trade, and `dueForFollowUpRow(page)` then resolves to two rows, turning every subsequent assertion/click on it into a Playwright strict-mode violation rather than a clean, debuggable failure. Non-blocking: doesn't affect the documented, actually-used CI/routine run path (confirmed clean on a real `make e2e` run as part of this PR's review), only the interactive UI-mode debugging workflow the e2e-test skill itself already calls out as non-routine; and the failure mode is loud (an exception), not a silent false pass. Worth a defensive tweak later (e.g. scope the seed's assertion to accept/clean up a pre-existing due TSLA row, mirroring the sibling block's own pattern) for consistency and smoother interactive debugging.

decisions.decision: Closed this task's `FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx` flake checklist item as resolved via a shared root cause confirmed while working backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups (a separate, overlapping investigation of the same symptom on this file plus `AddPositionDialog.test.tsx`, filed from PR #275's review): both are the same `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` failure caused by vitest's default `pool: 'forks'` spawning one forked worker process per test file with no cap (84 workers observed on a high-core-count host), which starves real-timer-driven `userEvent` interactions in these MUI-dialog tests under CPU contention. Fixed by capping `test.maxWorkers: 4` in `frontend/vite.config.ts` -- reproduced the failure 5/5 times on a 24-core devcontainer under the old unmodified config, then 0/7 across repeated full-suite runs after the cap. See backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups's own `decisions` entry for the full investigation (including why `pool: 'vmThreads'` and a bare timeout bump were rejected).
decisions.rationale: This task's earlier 13-isolated + 3-full-suite-rerun investigation found zero repro because none of those runs happened to combine a high enough default worker count with the specific interaction-heavy test to trigger contention -- it wasn't actually a one-off fluke, just an intermittent effect that needed the right (high-core-count) host to show up reliably, which the later PR #275 baseline run and this task's own reruns on the current host both did. Recording the shared fix here (rather than only on backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups) so a future reader of this task's checklist doesn't re-open the same investigation from zero. This task's other two checklist items (the `isoDateWeeksAgo` duplication and the `test.describe.serial` due-trade-seeding edge case) are unrelated findings from the same PR #249 review and are left untouched -- out of scope for this cross-reference.

decisions.decision: Extracted `isoDateWeeksAgo` to a new file `frontend/tests/dateFixtures.ts`, at the `tests/` root rather than inside `tests/mocks/` or `tests/e2e/`, and updated both `tests/mocks/handlers.ts` and `tests/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts` to import it from there. For the second checklist item, made `seedDueForFollowUpTrade` (in `tests/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts`) call a new helper `clearPreexistingDueFollowUpTrades` first, which GETs `/api/portfolio/closed-trades?due_for_follow_up=true`, filters to `FOLLOW_UP_TICKER` (TSLA), and POSTs a follow-up review for each match before the fresh due trade is seeded -- the 'clean up a pre-existing due TSLA row' option the checklist item itself named, rather than the 'accept' option (an accept-only fix would need `dueForFollowUpRow` and every downstream click/assertion in the block to handle an ambiguous 2-row match, which is a bigger, less local change than clearing the strays at seed time).
decisions.rationale: Location for the shared helper: no existing convention in this repo shares a helper across `tests/mocks/` (vitest/MSW) and `tests/e2e/` (Playwright) layers, but both `tsconfig.app.json` and vitest's config already include the whole `tests/` directory (not just `tests/src/` or similar), and several other cross-cutting helpers (`renderWithProviders.tsx`, `renderWithTheme.tsx`, `mockMatchMedia.ts`, `setup.ts`) already live directly at `tests/` root rather than nested under a layer-specific subdirectory -- `tests/dateFixtures.ts` follows that existing pattern rather than inventing a new `tests/shared/` directory for a single one-function file. Rejected keeping it under `tests/mocks/` and having the e2e spec import across that boundary: `tests/mocks/` is MSW-specific tooling (its own `server.ts` sets up vitest-only interception), so importing from it into a Playwright spec would be a confusing, one-directional dependency on a directory named for a concept (mocking) the e2e suite explicitly doesn't use. Rejected the 'accept a pre-existing due row' alternative for the second item because, unlike the sibling MSFT block (where 'Added' vs 'Merged' is a one-line assertion swap), tolerating a genuine second matching row here would require every one of `dueForFollowUpRow`'s several call sites across all three tests in the block to pick a specific one deterministically, which is more invasive than clearing the leftover state once at seed time. Verified the cleanup path actually works (not just that it's a no-op on a clean DB, which the routine `make e2e` run alone would not have caught) by manually seeding a stray unreviewed due TSLA trade against a locally-run fixture-mode backend and confirming the same GET-then-POST sequence clears it to zero before re-seeding.
